Yes, but only with `--dry-run`:

```bash
python scripts/export.py --env staging --dry-run
```

**Why:** the project's memory has a recorded hazard: in staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the **production** bucket. A real staging run would write into prod. I couldn't confirm this from the repo, since the bucket value comes from the staging environment, not from code. The script reads it at `scripts/export.py:10` and only falls back to `ledgerline-exports-dev` when the variable isn't set.

As `scripts/export.py` stands, the script only prints `exporting staging to <bucket> (dry_run=...)` and doesn't upload anything, so even a run without the flag would be harmless today. Keep using `--dry-run` anyway, because the hazard applies as soon as real upload logic is added. Also, the script never checks the `--dry-run` flag itself, so any upload code added later will need to respect it explicitly.

The printed line is a useful check: it shows which bucket staging actually resolves to, so you can see whether it's still the prod bucket.
